# TypeScript best practices

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

Examples: `references/patterns.md`.

# Type System Discipline

Make the compiler reject impossible states, mismatched primitives, and unhandled variants. Prefer defining errors and special cases out of existence over proliferating handlers. For TypeScript syntax, see the `typescript-best-practices` skill.

- **Brand semantic primitives.** `UserId` and `OrderId` are strings underneath but should not be interchangeable. Give each its own type, such as a branded intersection in TypeScript or a newtype elsewhere. Validate once at creation, trust the type downstream. If two arguments share a primitive type but mean different things, brand them.
- **External data is untyped until parsed.** RPC payloads, JSON, IPC messages, CLI args, config files, environment variables, database rows. Have a parse function at every boundary that turns unstructured input into the typed model. The **boundary-discipline** principle skill says where to put validation.
- **Derive types from authoritative schemas.** When a protocol buffer, OpenAPI spec, GraphQL schema, database migration, design-token file, or another file owns a shape, derive from it instead of hand-rolling a parallel type. See the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.
# Exposed UI

Import components and public types from the `src/lib/ui/index.ts` barrel (for example `./lib/ui` from `src/Example.svelte`). Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. It includes tokens, actions, patterns, focus rings, hidden captions, highlighted text and animation prerequisites. Field and Notice keep scoped styles. `/design-system` is the interactive reference in development only and requires no declarations API. Production returns 404 and hides its footer link.

Features own amounts, availability, chart geometry, URLs, analytics and async work. UI accepts formatted strings and presentation models. Pages own grids and section spacing. Use the [composition recipes](COMPOSITION.md) for native rows, declarations and identities.

| Component                              | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Button, ButtonLink                     | `variant` primary/secondary/quiet/subtle; `size` regular/large/compact/inline. Native attributes and handlers pass through. Button defaults to `type="button"`; links require `href`.                                                |
| Field                                  | Required visible `label`; `type` text/search/date/email; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native attributes reach the input; `class` reaches the wrapper. |
| Textarea | Required visible `label`; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native textarea attributes pass through; `class` reaches the wrapper. Resizes vertically. |
| SearchField                            | Required `label`, `help` snippet and `onclear`; bindable string `value` and native `input` reference; optional `shortcut`. Native attributes including `class` reach the input. Caller owns query behavior and focus restoration.    |
| Notice                                 | `tone` neutral/accent/warning. Native div attributes pass through. Caller chooses announcement `role`.                                                                                                                               |
| Badge                                  | `variant` result (default), profile or legend. `class` adds a root hook without replacing appearance.                                                                                                                                |
| MessageState                           | Required `title`; `variant` centered (default) or detail; `level` 1/2 changes semantics independently of appearance. Optional `icon`, `children`, `actions`, `role`, additive root `class`.                                          |
| SectionHeading                         | Required `id`, `title`; optional `level` 1/2/3 and trailing children. Heading presentation stays independent of rank.                                                                                                                |
| Disclosure                             | Required `summary`, children; `variant` names (default) or plain. Native details attributes, additive root `class`, bindable `open`.                                                                                                 |
| Metric                                 | Required `label`, formatted `value`; optional `regionLabel`, `available`, `description`, `level` 2/3. `variant` default or expanded; optional `align` start/end overrides variant and responsive text alignment. Available values remain keyboard-scrollable regions; unavailable text remains ordinary text.    |
| DeclarationCard                        | Required `heading`, `registered`, children snippets. `variant` default or compact changes padding.                                                                                                                                   |
| ValueRow                               | Required `source` and `value` snippets. Owns its `li` layout, including outside `.funding-list`; nested lists retain native layout.                                                                                                  |
| DataTable                              | Required text `caption`, `head` snippet and body children. Callers supply native rows, cells, scope and column-specific classes. No numeric alignment or column widths are assumed.                                                  |
| IdentityHeader                         | Required `name`, `kind`, `metadata`; optional `values`, `navigation`, `level` 1/2/3.                                                                                                                                                 |
| ResultRow, DeclarationList             | Native `li` and `ol` wrappers; children and optional accessible `label`. ResultRow callers supply their own anchor and may add a root `class` for a local palette.                                                                   |
| SignedBarList                          | `bars: SignedBar[]`, `baseline`; `variant` default or compact. Values are formatted strings; widths and signs come from features.                                                                                                    |
| BarChart, PieChart                     | Typed `ChartBar[]` geometry and `PieSlice[]` presentation data. Features calculate shares, signs and totals. See [RegistrationTimeline](../../RegistrationTimeline.svelte) and [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte).          |
| ViewLinks, ViewLink, Pagination        | Native navigation. Callers own destinations/current page; Pagination owns bound availability.                                                                                                                                        |
| Icon, IconIndicator                    | Canonical `IconName`; Icon is decorative. IconIndicator owns focus, pointer and Escape hints.                                                                                                                                        |
| HighlightedText, Spinner, SkeletonRows | Literal text highlights and decorative progress.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The first DataTable body row has a top divider, including when callers visually hide column headings.

Classes on native-attribute components accept Svelte class arrays and objects. Where a structural component exposes `class`, it adds a root hook. No class replacement API is supported. Use finite variants for existing appearances; caller-authored snippet classes own feature text and arrangements. The recipes show those classes explicitly.

Tokens in [tokens.css](tokens.css) own colors, spacing, type and focus. Override `--accent` on a container for another palette, such as `var(--accent-funder)`. The Exposed wordmark stays white across entity contexts. The landing heading uses member purple for MPs and funder teal for financial interests. Entity indicators, badges, highlights, charts and declared values derive their colors from the local accent; a ResultRow root `class` can select that palette explicitly. Actions use neutral `--action`, `--action-ink`, `--action-border`, `--action-surface` and `--action-hover`; all focus rings use `--focus-color`, independently of entity palettes. Keep action and focus tokens neutral in member and funder containers. `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` apply at the root or on a container. Native links, buttons and summaries add one pixel to the offset. Do not import internal stylesheets individually.

The [barrel](index.ts) is the public inventory. The gallery covers native disclosure/input behavior, precise metric overflow, repeated association IDs and pointer tooltip lifecycle. Financial parsing and availability decisions belong in feature adapters, never in UI components.

UI-owned snippet classes are `.results-list` (list reset and divider), `.entity-text` (shrinkable content), `.entity-name` (result anchor typography and hover), `.entity-alias` (secondary result text), `.funding-list` (nested list reset and spacing), `.declaration-reference`, `.payment-type`, `.currency-label`, `.empty-entry` (declaration context), `.amount` (exact value typography), and `.entry-count`/`.partial-note` (secondary chart/table text). These work with the single UI stylesheet import. Feature grids and custom table columns stay in callers.

`CategoryWheel` accepts `CategoryWheelOption[]` with caller-owned closed SVG sector `path`, open outer-boundary `rimPath` in the same local coordinates, and label positions, a selected identity, accessible group `label`, optional pixel `size` (default 284), and `onselect`. Native pressed buttons cover the complete sectors. Muted category surfaces, icons, labels and fine inner/radial boundaries stay constant. Selection brightens only the outer rim; focus uses a neutral full-sector outline. A decorative neutral chart glyph occupies the center. Each option has a 142px-wide native button and optional `height` (default 142px). Taller sectors must provide their full height so the native hit target covers the path. Features provide a size that fits the layout.

`RankingList` accepts formatted `RankingRow[]` and an accessible list `label`. Features supply stable keys, destinations, amounts, coverage, signs and bar widths. The list animates row and bar entry and disables animation for reduced motion. Party identities can omit destinations.
# Composition recipes

Each example is a complete Svelte component placed at `src/Example.svelte`. Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. These examples use static presentation data; production features supply real URLs and formatted values.

Actions and focus remain neutral in every entity context. Override `--accent` only for entity meaning, such as funder badges, highlights and charts.

## Search result

`ResultRow` renders `li`. The caller owns the anchor, metadata and list container. The UI stylesheet owns `.entity-text`, `.entity-name` and `.entity-alias`.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { ResultRow, Badge, IconIndicator } from "./lib/ui";
</script>

<ul class="results-list">
  <ResultRow label="Example Foundation, funder">
    <IconIndicator icon="building" label="Organisation" />
    <div class="entity-text">
      <a
        class="entity-name"
        href="/funders/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
        >Example Foundation</a
      >
      <span class="entity-alias">Also recorded as Example Trust</span>
    </div>
    <Badge>Organisation</Badge>
  </ResultRow>
</ul>
```

## Declaration and value

`DeclarationList` renders `ol`, `DeclarationCard` renders `li`, and `ValueRow` renders a nested `li`. `.funding-list` is the UI list recipe for reset and spacing. The registered snippet is already wrapped in `p`, so supply inline content. The UI stylesheet owns `.payment-type` and `.amount`; the caller supplies the formatted amount.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { DeclarationList, DeclarationCard, ValueRow } from "./lib/ui";
</script>

<DeclarationList label="Example declarations">
  <DeclarationCard>
    {#snippet heading()}<h3>Employment and earnings</h3>{/snippet}
    {#snippet registered()}<time datetime="2026-01-20">20 January 2026</time
      >{/snippet}
    <ul class="funding-list">
      <ValueRow>
        {#snippet source()}
          <a href="/funders/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
            >Example Foundation</a
          >
          <span class="payment-type">Consultancy</span>
        {/snippet}
        {#snippet value()}<span class="amount">£1,234.56</span>{/snippet}
      </ValueRow>
    </ul>
  </DeclarationCard>
</DeclarationList>
```

## Identity and metric

`IdentityHeader` owns its title, metadata paragraph and grid. Supply inline metadata and a native navigation composition. `.identity-totals` is caller-owned grid placement. `Metric` takes exact formatted strings without interpreting money.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import {
    IdentityHeader,
    Badge,
    Icon,
    Metric,
    ViewLinks,
    ViewLink,
  } from "./lib/ui";
</script>

<IdentityHeader name="Jane Example">
  {#snippet kind()}<Badge variant="profile"><Icon name="parliament" />MP</Badge
    >{/snippet}
  {#snippet metadata()}Example Party<span>Example constituency</span>{/snippet}
  {#snippet values()}
    <div class="identity-totals">
      <Metric variant="expanded" label="Declared amounts" value="£1,234.56" />
    </div>
  {/snippet}
  {#snippet navigation()}
    <ViewLinks label="Example views">
      <ViewLink href="/members/1" aria-current="page">Summary</ViewLink>
      <ViewLink href="/members/1/history">Declaration history</ViewLink>
    </ViewLinks>
  {/snippet}
</IdentityHeader>

<style>
  .identity-totals {
    grid-column: 1 / -1;
    min-width: 0;
  }
</style>
```

## Native table columns

`DataTable` supplies the caption, `thead`, `tbody` and neutral cell rules. Use actual `th`/`td` classes in the caller for widths and numeric alignment. [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte) is the production example. It owns `.recipient-name` and `.recipient-total`; those classes are not reusable UI APIs.

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application

## Domain terminology

Use these meanings consistently in code, documentation, and UI copy.

- **Declarations** are records of financial interests registered by a member.
  A declaration belongs to a category and can contain zero, one, or multiple
  funding entries. A declaration count is not a payment or funding-entry count.
  Registration dates do not necessarily describe when money changed hands.
- **Members** are people identified by their Parliament member ID. Public MP
  pages use that identity. Stored records can include former members, and the
  latest stored party or constituency does not establish affiliation at the
  time of a declaration.
- **Funding** refers to the payments, support, rates, loans, gifts, or other
  benefits recorded within declarations. A funding entry is one source
  occurrence, even when another entry has identical values. Funding can have
  no known amount or resolved funder. Support linked to a member can go to a
  party organisation rather than to the member personally.
- **Rankings** are ordered comparisons of declared GBP amounts in the imported
  data, not measures of income or wealth.

**Note**: users may use the word _earnings_ when prompting. You should understand this to mean all funding sources.

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev):
  - `wt switch --create <branch-name> --base main`
- Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

## Frontend coding policy

All frontend changes must follow this policy, including prototype UI. UI edits
must preserve the financial totals contract above. The design-system rules are
required acceptance criteria for new UI and changes to existing UI.

### UI copy scope

- Add only the visible text needed for the requested interaction or data.
  Do not add unrequested subtitles, helper paragraphs, explanatory labels,
  badges, or repeated context to make a feature feel complete.
- Reuse existing wording. Keep required control labels, accessible names,
  error messages, and the financial wording required above.
- Before committing UI changes, review each added visible string against the
  request. Remove optional copy that the user did not request. A component
  example is not permission to copy its explanatory text into a feature.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Omit unrequested visible UI copy. | Review added strings in the diff against the user's request. This is a judgment check; types and automated tests cannot determine whether copy was requested. |

### Client and server

- Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local
  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.
- Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access
  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.
- Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests
  go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API.
- Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK
  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

### PostHog

- Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development
  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.
- Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather
  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

### Design system

- You must read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding or
  changing UI. Follow their component contracts and composition patterns.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- You must import shared UI components and types from
  `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the appropriate relative path. Load
  `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the root layout. Do not import
  component internals or internal stylesheets directly.
- You must reuse existing components, composition patterns, and typed variants.
  Do not recreate shared controls or patterns in feature components. When a
  reusable capability is missing, extend the design system before using it
  in a feature.
- You must use design-system tokens for colors, spacing, typography, and focus.
  Do not substitute hard-coded values for those tokens. Purple identifies MPs,
  teal identifies funders, and utility icons use the muted neutral color.
  Actions and focus indicators must stay neutral in every entity context.
- Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features.
  Shared UI must accept presentation models without interpreting money or
  fetching data. Feature CSS must be limited to page arrangement and
  caller-authored content. Do not target shared component internals or override
  their appearance through global selectors or replacement classes. Use the
  documented typed variants and additive root hooks.
- You must implement reusable additions in `frontend/src/lib/ui`, export them
  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

| Rule | Enforcement |

# TypeScript best practices

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

Examples: `references/patterns.md`.

# Type System Discipline

Make the compiler reject impossible states, mismatched primitives, and unhandled variants. Prefer defining errors and special cases out of existence over proliferating handlers. For TypeScript syntax, see the `typescript-best-practices` skill.

- **Brand semantic primitives.** `UserId` and `OrderId` are strings underneath but should not be interchangeable. Give each its own type, such as a branded intersection in TypeScript or a newtype elsewhere. Validate once at creation, trust the type downstream. If two arguments share a primitive type but mean different things, brand them.
- **External data is untyped until parsed.** RPC payloads, JSON, IPC messages, CLI args, config files, environment variables, database rows. Have a parse function at every boundary that turns unstructured input into the typed model. The **boundary-discipline** principle skill says where to put validation.
- **Derive types from authoritative schemas.** When a protocol buffer, OpenAPI spec, GraphQL schema, database migration, design-token file, or another file owns a shape, derive from it instead of hand-rolling a parallel type. See the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.
# Exposed UI

Import components and public types from the `src/lib/ui/index.ts` barrel (for example `./lib/ui` from `src/Example.svelte`). Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. It includes tokens, actions, patterns, focus rings, hidden captions, highlighted text and animation prerequisites. Field and Notice keep scoped styles. `/design-system` is the interactive reference in development only and requires no declarations API. Production returns 404 and hides its footer link.

Features own amounts, availability, chart geometry, URLs, analytics and async work. UI accepts formatted strings and presentation models. Pages own grids and section spacing. Use the [composition recipes](COMPOSITION.md) for native rows, declarations and identities.

| Component                              | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| Field                                  | Required visible `label`; `type` text/search/date/email; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native attributes reach the input; `class` reaches the wrapper. |
| Textarea | Required visible `label`; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native textarea attributes pass through; `class` reaches the wrapper. Resizes vertically. |
| SearchField                            | Required `label`, `help` snippet and `onclear`; bindable string `value` and native `input` reference; optional `shortcut`. Native attributes including `class` reach the input. Caller owns query behavior and focus restoration.    |
| Notice                                 | `tone` neutral/accent/warning. Native div attributes pass through. Caller chooses announcement `role`.                                                                                                                               |
| Badge                                  | `variant` result (default), profile or legend. `class` adds a root hook without replacing appearance.                                                                                                                                |
| MessageState                           | Required `title`; `variant` centered (default) or detail; `level` 1/2 changes semantics independently of appearance. Optional `icon`, `children`, `actions`, `role`, additive root `class`.                                          |

Available values remain keyboard-scrollable regions; unavailable text remains ordinary text.    |
| DeclarationCard                        | Required `heading`, `registered`, children snippets. `variant` default or compact changes padding.                                                                                                                                   |
| ValueRow                               | Required `source` and `value` snippets. Owns its `li` layout, including outside `.funding-list`; nested lists retain native layout.                                                                                                  |

| ViewLinks, ViewLink, Pagination        | Native navigation. Callers own destinations/current page; Pagination owns bound availability.                                                                                                                                        |

| HighlightedText, Spinner, SkeletonRows | Literal text highlights and decorative progress.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The first DataTable body row has a top divider, including when callers visually hide column headings.

Classes on native-attribute components accept Svelte class arrays and objects. Where a structural component exposes `class`, it adds a root hook. No class replacement API is supported. Use finite variants for existing appearances; caller-authored snippet classes own feature text and arrangements. The recipes show those classes explicitly.

Tokens in [tokens.css](tokens.css) own colors, spacing, type and focus. Override `--accent` on a container for another palette, such as `var(--accent-funder)`. The Exposed wordmark stays white across entity contexts. The landing heading uses member purple for MPs and funder teal for financial interests. Entity indicators, badges, highlights, charts and declared values derive their colors from the local accent; a ResultRow root `class` can select that palette explicitly. Actions use neutral `--action`, `--action-ink`, `--action-border`, `--action-surface` and `--action-hover`; all focus rings use `--focus-color`, independently of entity palettes. Keep action and focus tokens neutral in member and funder containers. `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` apply at the root or on a container. Native links, buttons and summaries add one pixel to the offset. Do not import internal stylesheets individually.

The [barrel](index.ts) is the public inventory. The gallery covers native disclosure/input behavior, precise metric overflow, repeated association IDs and pointer tooltip lifecycle. Financial parsing and availability decisions belong in feature adapters, never in UI components.

UI-owned snippet classes are `.results-list` (list reset and divider), `.entity-text` (shrinkable content), `.entity-name` (result anchor typography and hover), `.entity-alias` (secondary result text), `.funding-list` (nested list reset and spacing), `.declaration-reference`, `.payment-type`, `.currency-label`, `.empty-entry` (declaration context), `.amount` (exact value typography), and `.entry-count`/`.partial-note` (secondary chart/table text). Selection brightens only the outer rim; focus uses a neutral full-sector outline. A decorative neutral chart glyph occupies the center. Each option has a 142px-wide native button and optional `height` (default 142px). Taller sectors must provide their full height so the native hit target covers the path. Features provide a size that fits the layout.

`RankingList` accepts formatted `RankingRow[]` and an accessible list `label`. Features supply stable keys, destinations, amounts, coverage, signs and bar widths. The list animates row and bar entry and disables animation for reduced motion. Party identities can omit destinations.
